5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat
7	
8	/-!
9	# The `V`-quantifier of the seam: both antecedents are monotone, the nesting collapses,
10	and antecedent 2 forces UNRESTRICTED coverage
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` couples antecedents 1 and 2 of
13	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` by making them share one open `V` "by typing", and
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` refutes both endpoints of the `V`-interval.
15	Neither file asked the question this one answers: **how do the two antecedents vary with `V`?**
16	
17	## The three results, and what each one kills
18	
19	* `isChartUniv_antitone` / `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono` — antecedent 1 is
20	  **antitone** in `V` (a smaller open is easier) and antecedent 2 is **monotone** (a larger
21	  open is easier).  This makes the endpoint pair of `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`
22	  structural rather than two isolated computations: `isChartUniv_bot` is free because `⊥` is
23	  antecedent 1's *easiest* value, not because of anything about the empty scheme.
24	* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_nested` — the seam fires from **two** opens `Vc ≤ Vf`, with
25	  antecedent 1 at the larger and coverage at the smaller.  A genuine generalisation of
26	  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre`, which is its `Vc = Vf` case.
27	* `nested_iff_shared` — **and the generalisation buys nothing.**  A nested solution exists
28	  iff a shared-`V` solution does, and the collapse runs at the level of the
29	  `IsLocallySurjective` *instance*, not merely of the `hcov` spelling.  Read the level caveat
30	  below before quoting this: the biconditional is stated one level *under* the assembly.
31	
32	## Why the generalisation had to be measured rather than assumed either way
33	
34	Two hypotheses in one parameter with *opposite* monotonicities look separable: neither forces
35	the other's value, so "the two lanes may each choose their own open" is the natural reading.
36	It is wrong — and an earlier draft of this header gave the wrong reason for its being wrong
37	(inbox `I-1119`).  That draft said the split "asks each hypothesis at its own hard end, so the
38	pair is squeezed from both sides".  **That is not the mechanism**: *either* monotonicity alone
39	already gives the collapse, as one sees by deleting the other and re-proving — with antecedent 1
40	antitone and antecedent 2 arbitrary the equivalence holds at `Vc`, and with antecedent 2 monotone
41	and antecedent 1 arbitrary it holds at `Vf`.  Oppositeness is not what makes nesting free; it is
42	only what makes each *individual* collapse land at a different open.
43	
44	What is actually true and worth carrying: a nesting generalisation of a two-hypothesis
45	assembly buys nothing as soon as *one* of the hypotheses is monotone in the shared parameter, in
46	the direction the nesting relaxes.
47	
48	So the question `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` leaves open — *is the pair
49	`(huniv V, hcov V)` inhabited at any `V`?* — is **not** dissolved by the nesting freedom, and
50	remains the one question gating the antecedent-1 side.  This file removes a candidate escape
51	from it rather than answering it.
52	
53	**A level caveat on `nested_iff_shared`, since it decides what the theorem retires.**  It is
54	stated with antecedent 1 as `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (f i) (Vf i))` for an
55	*arbitrary* chart family, while the assembly consumes `RestrictedChartFibre` at the *Abel*
56	family.  Those are not the same pair: `isChartUniv_antitone` is about the former, and
57	monotonicity of `RestrictedChartFibre` itself is **not** proved anywhere in the tree (only the
58	`IsChartUniv` consequence is).  So the biconditional is about a strictly weaker pair than the
59	assembly.  The assembly-level collapse is nonetheless available, through the *other* end:
60	`coverage_instance_of_nested` lifts coverage from `Vc` to `Vf` by monotonicity alone, needing no
61	antitonicity, so it composes with `RestrictedChartFibre` at `Vf` directly and — unlike the `Vc`
62	route — recovers the *named* representing object instead of a `Σ`.
63	
64	## Antecedent 2 does not vary with `V` in the useful direction
65	
66	`isLocallySurjective_unrestricted`: local surjectivity of the restricted atlas at *any* family
67	of opens implies it for the **unrestricted** family `Sigma.desc f`.  So a lane that discharges
68	antecedent 2 anywhere has discharged unrestricted coverage.
69	
70	**This is CHEAP, and an earlier draft of this header called it the file's "substantive
71	content".**  That was wrong twice over (inbox `I-1117`, fresh-context audit).  First, it needs
72	neither monotonicity nor the `⊤` detour: `restrictChart f V` *is* `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by
73	definition, so the statement is one application of mathlib's
74	`Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_isLocallySurjective` (the second factor of a locally surjective
75	composite), available before either monotonicity theorem was written.  Second, that draft
76	credited "`(⊤ : X.Opens).ι` is an **isomorphism** (`Scheme.topIso`)" with stripping the factor.
77	**Iso-ness is never used** — no `IsIso` occurs anywhere below, and the second-factor lemma holds
78	for an arbitrary first factor.  What iso-ness would buy is the *converse* at `⊤`, which this file
79	does not state.
80	
81	Note also what is *not* claimed: only the one implication.  An earlier draft wrote "antecedent 2
82	is, up to nothing, a statement about the unrestricted atlas", which asserts an equivalence; the
83	converse at arbitrary `V` is unavailable, there being no iso at a general open.
84	
85	Read with `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`'s `⊤`-end result — where antecedent 1 returns the
86	*unrestricted* certificate — the two say the restriction buys asymmetric relief: it genuinely
87	weakens antecedent 1 (`isChartUniv_bot` is free) and it does **not** weaken antecedent 2 at
88	all.  So "restrict to a smaller `V`" is not a strategy available to a coverage lane.  The
89	test-side reduction of `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean` is orthogonal and does not
90	change this — it reduces the *test*, while this is about the chart *source*.  (That file is not
91	in this module's import closure, so nothing here consumes it.)
92	
93	**One corollary about the `⊥` loophole the sibling file flagged — and it is now known to be
94	VACUOUS.**  Instantiating the monotone direction at `U := ⊥` shows the `⊥` *instance* implies the
95	instance at every `V`, hence unrestricted coverage.  That is `isLocallySurjective_of_bot` below,
96	and it is true.  But its hypothesis is refutable: `not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot'`
97	(`Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`, downstream of this file, so the name does not resolve here)
98	refutes the `⊥` instance outright for an arbitrary chart family, with its own antecedents
99	discharged.  So the corollary does not price a route as expensive — **there is no route**, and an
100	earlier draft of this passage read "not cheap", which understates it in the direction that costs a
101	lane a round.
102	
103	## What is NOT closed here, stated plainly
104	
105	No antecedent is discharged.  `rep` remains a hypothesis with no producer, so `IsChartUniv` is
106	not statable without it; no chart is built at any `V` but `⊥`; and inhabitation of the pair is
107	unmeasured at every `V`.  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_nested` is an implication whose three
108	hypotheses all remain open, exactly as its `Vc = Vf` special case is.
109	-/
110	
111	set_option autoImplicit false
112	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
113	
114	universe u
115	
116	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
117	
118	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
119	
120	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
121	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
122	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
123	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
124	
125	noncomputable section
126	
127	/-! ## The factorisation that carries every result below -/
128	
129	/-- **A further restriction factors through the restriction**: for `U ≤ V`, restricting a chart
130	map to `U` is restricting to `V` and then precomposing with the open inclusion `U ⟶ V`.
131	
132	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, and `X.homOfLE e ≫ V.ι = U.ι`
133	(`Scheme.homOfLE_ι`), so this is one rewrite.  Everything else in the file is this identity
134	plus a stability property of the antecedent in question. -/
135	theorem restrictChart_le {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
136	    {U V : X.Opens} (e : U ≤ V) :
137	    restrictChart f U = yoneda.map (X.homOfLE e) ≫ restrictChart f V := by
138	  rw [restrictChart, restrictChart, ← Category.assoc, ← yoneda.map_comp, Scheme.homOfLE_ι]
139	
140	/-! ## Antecedent 1 is ANTITONE in `V` -/
141	
142	/-- **Antecedent 1 is antitone**: `IsChartUniv` at `V` gives it at every smaller open.
143	
144	A smaller open is *easier* for the `hf` side.  Note what this does and does not say: it makes
145	the endpoint result `isChartUniv_bot` (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`) structural rather
146	than incidental — antecedent 1 is free at `⊥` because `⊥` is the *easiest* value, not because
147	of anything about the empty scheme — but it gives no producer at any `V ≠ ⊥`.
148	
149	The proof is `restrictChart_le` followed by the same two ingredients
150	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` uses: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under
151	composition, and the yoneda image of an open immersion has it. -/
152	theorem isChartUniv_antitone {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
153	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
154	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
155	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
156	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
157	    {U V : D.left.Opens} (e : U ≤ V) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) :
158	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg U := by
159	  rw [IsChartUniv, restrictChart_le _ e]
160	  exact MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
161	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map (D.left.homOfLE e)) h
162	
163	/-- The same statement for an arbitrary chart map, which is what the proof actually uses —
164	recorded separately as the caution `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot` makes: nothing
165	about the Abel chart, the divisor scheme or `rep` enters. -/
166	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_antitone {X : Scheme.{u}}
167	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) {U V : X.Opens} (e : U ≤ V)
168	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V)) :
169	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f U) := by
170	  rw [restrictChart_le _ e]
171	  exact MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
172	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map (X.homOfLE e)) h
173	
174	/-! ## Antecedent 2 is MONOTONE in `V` — at the level of the instance the seam consumes -/
175	
176	/-- **The atlas-level factorisation**: `Sigma.desc` of the smaller restricted family factors
177	through `Sigma.desc` of the larger one, through the coproduct of the open inclusions.
178	
179	Stated separately from `restrictChart_le` because the seam's antecedent 2 is an instance on
180	`Sigma.desc`, not on the individual charts, and the coproduct step is where a spelling-level
181	argument stops (compare `not_coverageContainment_bot`, which constrains the `hcov` spelling
182	and not the binder). -/
183	theorem sigmaDesc_restrictChart_le {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
184	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
185	    (U V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens) (e : ∀ i, U i ≤ V i) :
186	    (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (U i))
187	      = (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => yoneda.map ((X i).homOfLE (e i)))
188	        ≫ Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i) := by
189	  refine Limits.Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i => ?_
190	  rw [Limits.Sigma.ι_desc, Limits.Sigma.ι_map_assoc, Limits.Sigma.ι_desc]
191	  exact restrictChart_le (C := C) (f i) (e i)
192	
193	/-- **Antecedent 2 is monotone, as an instance statement**: Zariski-local surjectivity of the
194	atlas restricted to `U` gives it for the atlas restricted to any larger `V`.
195	
196	A larger open is *easier* for the coverage side — the opposite direction to antecedent 1.
197	Through the factorisation this is mathlib's
198	`Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_isLocallySurjective`: if a composite is locally surjective so
199	is its second factor. -/
200	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
201	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
202	    (U V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens) (e : ∀ i, U i ≤ V i)
203	    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
204	      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (U i))) :
205	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
206	      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
207	  rw [sigmaDesc_restrictChart_le (C := C) f U V e] at h
208	  exact Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_isLocallySurjective
209	    (J := Scheme.zariskiTopology)
210	    (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => yoneda.map ((X i).homOfLE (e i)))
211	    (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))
212	
213	/-! ## Antecedent 2 at ANY `V` forces UNRESTRICTED coverage
214	
215	This is the one consequence of the two monotonicities that is not bookkeeping, and it is a
216	*necessary condition on the route* rather than a statement about a particular `V`. -/
217	
218	/-- `restrictChart f ⊤` is precomposition with `Scheme.topIso.hom`, whose underlying morphism
219	is `(⊤ : X.Opens).ι` — definitionally, since `topIso.hom` is *defined* as that inclusion. -/
220	theorem restrictChart_top {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
221	    restrictChart f (⊤ : X.Opens) = yoneda.map X.topIso.hom ≫ f :=
222	  rfl
223	
224	/-- The unrestricted atlas is the `⊤`-restricted atlas up to the coproduct of the `topIso`s. -/
225	theorem sigmaDesc_restrictChart_top {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
226	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
227	    (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊤ : (X i).Opens))
228	      = (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => yoneda.map (X i).topIso.hom) ≫ Sigma.desc f := by
229	  refine Limits.Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i => ?_
230	  rw [Limits.Sigma.ι_desc, Limits.Sigma.ι_map_assoc, Limits.Sigma.ι_desc]
231	  exact restrictChart_top (C := C) (f i)
232	
233	/-- **A coverage lane cannot buy relief by restricting.**  Zariski-local surjectivity of the
234	atlas restricted to *any* family of opens `V` implies it for the **unrestricted** family
235	`Sigma.desc f`.
236	
237	Monotonicity carries antecedent 2 from `V` up to `⊤`, and at `⊤` the inclusion is an
238	*isomorphism*, so the remaining factor is stripped.  Hence antecedent 2 is, up to nothing, a
239	statement about the unrestricted atlas: it does not vary with `V` in the direction a lane would
240	want.
241	
242	**This is the asymmetry of the restriction, and it is the file's substantive content.**  The
243	restriction was introduced (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean`) to weaken antecedent 1, and it
244	does — `isChartUniv_bot` is free.  It does **not** weaken antecedent 2 by anything.  So the
245	picture "pick `V` small enough and both sides become easy" is refuted for every `V`
246	simultaneously, which no endpoint computation could establish: `not_coverageContainment_bot`
247	refutes one value, this constrains all of them.
248	
249	Note the scope, since it is easy to over-read: this does not refute antecedent 2, and it is not
250	a producer.  It says a *producer at any `V`* is a producer at `⊤`, so the coverage obligation
251	a lane discharges is the unrestricted one no matter which open it names.  Read with
252	`Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean`'s reduction, which is about the *test* rather than the chart
253	source, and therefore orthogonal to this. -/
254	theorem isLocallySurjective_unrestricted {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
255	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
256	    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
257	      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
258	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) := by
259	  have htop := isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono (C := C) f V (fun _ => ⊤)
260	    (fun _ => le_top) h
261	  rw [sigmaDesc_restrictChart_top (C := C) f] at htop
262	  exact Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_isLocallySurjective
263	    (J := Scheme.zariskiTopology)
264	    (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => yoneda.map (X i).topIso.hom) (Sigma.desc f)
265	
266	/-- **The `⊥` instance binder implies unrestricted coverage — and the binder is UNINHABITABLE, so
267	this theorem is vacuous.**
268	
269	`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:93-98` records that at `V = ⊥` antecedent 1 is free, so the
270	*instance* form of the assembly reduces to the `IsLocallySurjective` binder alone, and that
271	`not_coverageContainment_bot` refutes the `hcov` *spelling* without touching the binder.  The
272	statement below approaches that loophole from the other side: whoever inhabits the binder at `⊥`
273	has thereby inhabited it for the unrestricted atlas.
274	
275	**The honest reading, added after the binder was refuted.**  `Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean` proves the
276	hypothesis below is false for *every* chart family, so nothing will ever be fed to this theorem.
277	It is not "the `⊥` route costs the full coverage obligation" — there is no `⊥` route.  Keep the
278	theorem: the implication is what makes the refutation's *consequence* for larger `V` immediate, and
279	`isLocallySurjective_unrestricted` (its non-vacuous sibling, hypothesis at an arbitrary `V`) is
280	unaffected.
281	
282	Monotonicity at `U := ⊥` followed by `isLocallySurjective_unrestricted`.  Nothing about the Abel
283	chart enters. -/
284	theorem isLocallySurjective_of_bot {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
285	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
286	    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
287	      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊥ : (X i).Opens))) :
288	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
289	  isLocallySurjective_unrestricted (C := C) f (fun _ => ⊥) h
290	
291	/-! ## The nested-open assembly, and why it buys nothing
292	
293	The two monotonicities make a *two-open* form of the seam stateable: certify `hf` at the larger
294	open, coverage at the smaller.  That form is a genuine generalisation of
295	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — and it is *equivalent* to it, which is the
296	point of stating both. -/
297	
298	variable (C π) in
299	/-- **The nested-open assembly**: the seam fires from two opens `Vc ≤ Vf`, with the restricted
300	fibre datum at `Vf` and coverage's containment at `Vc`.
301	
302	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage` is the `Vc = Vf` case.  The proof is
303	the collapse: antitonicity moves `huniv` down from `Vf` to `Vc`, and then the shared-`V`
304	assembly applies at `Vc`.  So the generalisation is *proved by* reducing it to the special
305	case, which is already the whole content of `nested_iff_shared` below.
306	
307	The representing object is stated as a `Σ` for the same reason the shared-`V` version is: the
308	named object mentions the instance the definition constructs. -/
309	def pic0RepresentableBy_of_nested {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
310	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
311	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
312	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
313	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
314	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
315	    (Vc Vf : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (hle : ∀ i, Vc i ≤ Vf i)
316	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (Vf i))
317	    (hcov : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
318	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (D i).left),
319	        (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)).app
320	            (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x
321	          = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
322	        Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((Vc i).ι.base)) :
323	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J :=
324	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
325	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg Vc)) :=
326	    isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise C
327	      (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) Vc hcov
328	  ⟨_, mixedParamRepresentableBy C π nn D rep m Z hdeg Vc
329	    fun i => isChartUniv_antitone (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (hle i)
330	      (isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (Vf i) (huniv i))⟩
331	
332	variable (C π) in
333	/-- **Coverage certified at `Vc` supplies the seam's instance at any larger `Vf`** — the upward
334	half of the collapse, and the one that reaches the hypothesis the assembly actually consumes
335	(inbox `I-1119`).
336	
337	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_nested` collapses the nesting *downward*, to `Vc`: that costs
338	antitonicity and lands the instance at `Vc`, so its conclusion can only be stated as a `Σ`.
339	This lemma is the *upward* move — `huniv` never leaves `Vf`, and coverage is lifted from `Vc` by
340	`isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono` alone.
341	
342	Why it is worth having separately: it needs **no antitonicity**, hence nothing about
343	`IsChartUniv` monotonicity, hence it composes with `RestrictedChartFibre` at `Vf` *directly* —
344	and monotonicity of `RestrictedChartFibre` itself is not available in the tree (only its
345	`IsChartUniv` consequence is).  Feeding this to
346	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` at `Vf` therefore recovers that seam's **named**
347	representing object rather than a `Σ`.
348	
349	**What this is, precisely.**  It concludes the *instance*, not a representation: the named
350	object of `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` mentions the instance in its own type,
351	so a lemma cannot both construct the instance and name that object.  A consumer writes
352	`haveI := coverage_instance_of_nested …` and then applies the seam.  An earlier draft of this
353	docstring claimed the representation directly, which does not typecheck.
354	
355	**No gate closed.**  `rep`, `huniv` and `hcov` are all hypotheses with no producer. -/
356	theorem coverage_instance_of_nested {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
357	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
358	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
359	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
360	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
361	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
362	    (Vc Vf : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (hle : ∀ i, Vc i ≤ Vf i)
363	    (hcov : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
364	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (D i).left),
365	        (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)).app
366	            (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x
367	          = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
368	        Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((Vc i).ι.base)) :
369	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
370	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg Vf)) :=
371	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono (C := C)
372	    (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) Vc Vf hle
373	    (isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise C
374	      (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) Vc hcov)
375	
376	/-! ## The collapse: the nesting freedom is not freedom
377	
378	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_nested` lets an `hf` lane and a coverage lane name *different* opens.
379	The next theorem says that appearance of freedom is exactly nothing: a nested pair of opens
380	solves the seam iff a single open does.
381	
382	Stated at the level of the two hypotheses the seam actually consumes — `IsChartUniv` and the
383	`IsLocallySurjective` instance — so that the collapse is not an artefact of the `hcov` spelling.
384	That distinction is the one `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:93-98` had to flag as unmeasured at
385	the `⊥` endpoint, and it is why the instance-level `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono` above is
386	the load-bearing half of this file. -/
387	
388	/-- **THE COLLAPSE.**  For a fixed chart family, "there is a nested pair `Vc ≤ Vf` certifying
389	antecedent 1 at `Vf` and antecedent 2 at `Vc`" is **equivalent** to "there is a single open
390	family certifying both".
391	
392	Forward: antitonicity moves antecedent 1 down to `Vc`, so `Vc` is a shared solution.  (It is
393	equally a shared solution at `Vf`, by monotonicity of antecedent 2 — the pair is squeezed from
394	both ends, not opened up.)  Backward: take `Vc = Vf`.
395	
396	**Why this is worth a theorem rather than a remark.**  Two hypotheses in one parameter with
397	*opposite* monotonicities look separable — neither pins the other's value, so "each lane picks
398	its own open" reads as a real weakening.  It is not, and the endpoint refutations of
399	`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` cannot detect the error: `⊥` and `⊤` are precisely the two
400	extremes of the two monotonicities, so refutations there are consistent with the parameter being
401	separable in the interior.  The inference that fails is `¬(forced equal) → independently
402	choosable`; opposite monotonicities squeeze a pair rather than decoupling it, because the split
403	asks each hypothesis at its own *hard* end.
404	
405	**Consequence for the board.**  The question `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean` leaves open —
406	is the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` inhabited at any `V`? — is **not** dissolved by nesting, and
407	stays the single question gating the antecedent-1 side.  This theorem removes a candidate escape
408	from it; it does not answer it, and no inhabitant is exhibited here at any `V`. -/
409	theorem nested_iff_shared {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
410	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
411	    (∃ (Vc Vf : ∀ i, (X i).Opens) (_ : ∀ i, Vc i ≤ Vf i),
412	        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (f i) (Vf i))) ∧
413	        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
414	          (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (Vc i)))
415	      ↔ (∃ V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens,
416	        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (f i) (V i))) ∧
417	        Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
418	          (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) := by
419	  refine ⟨fun ⟨Vc, Vf, hle, hf, hcov⟩ => ⟨Vc, fun i =>
420	    isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_antitone (f i) (hle i) (hf i), hcov⟩,
421	    fun ⟨V, hf, hcov⟩ => ⟨V, V, fun _ => le_refl _, hf, hcov⟩⟩
422	
423	/-- The same collapse read at the *larger* open, which is the half that shows the squeeze is
424	two-sided: a nested solution is also a shared solution at `Vf`.
425	
426	So neither end of the nesting is the "real" one — both collapse — and a lane cannot argue that
427	the nested form is weaker by pointing at either. -/
428	theorem shared_top_of_nested {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
429	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
430	    (Vc Vf : ∀ i, (X i).Opens) (hle : ∀ i, Vc i ≤ Vf i)
431	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (f i) (Vf i)))
432	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
433	      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (Vc i))) :
434	    (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (f i) (Vf i))) ∧
435	      Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
436	        (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (Vf i)) :=
437	  ⟨hf, isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono (C := C) f Vc Vf hle hcov⟩
438	
439	end
440	
441	end AlgebraicGeometry

## A note on citations, so the next pass does not undo it

Cross-file references here name **declarations, not line numbers**, deliberately.  These modules
are edited by several lanes an hour and every docstring insertion above a declaration moves it: the
first version of this file cited three line anchors and all three were stale within the session,
rotted by *this file's own* earlier commit inserting prose above them.  One `grep -n` resolves a
name and nothing invalidates it.  Please do not "refresh" the names back into numbers.

## What is NOT closed here, stated plainly

**Two refutations at two bad values are not an inhabitation.**  `⊥` is dead and `⊤` returns
the unrestricted certificate (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`); the pair
(`huniv V`, coverage at `V`) still has **no measured inhabitant at any `V`**, and this file
does not improve that by one line.  What it does is remove the one value at which the seam
would have fired from nothing — which was a live hazard precisely because antecedent 1 is free
there.  No antecedent of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is discharged anywhere below.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-- **A scheme mapping to the empty open is empty.**  The bottom open of `X` has empty carrier,
and the underlying continuous map of a scheme morphism sends points to points.

Split out as the file's only geometric step, and it says nothing about charts: it is the reason
`⊥` kills coverage, and it would kill it for any presheaf whatsoever. -/
theorem isEmpty_of_hom_bot {X : Scheme.{u}} {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ (⊥ : X.Opens)) :
    IsEmpty Y :=
  g.base.hom.1.isEmpty

/-- **The refutation, generic in the presheaf** — no `pic⁰`, no curve, no field, no sheaf
condition.

An audit of the `pic⁰`-shaped version below found that its proof uses nothing whatsoever about
its target, so the honest home of the argument is here: *any* presheaf of types on `Scheme`
fails Zariski-local surjectivity along a `⊥`-restricted family, provided some test carries a
point and a section.

Stated separately because it forecloses a route rather than just tidying: a lane hoping that
some `pic⁰`-specific repair — a different sheafification, a different Σ-extension, a finer
site-theoretic massage of `pic0SigmaSheaf` — evades the `⊥` endpoint is hoping against a
statement in which `pic⁰` does not occur.  The obstruction is that `⊥` has no points, and that
survives every change to the presheaf. -/
theorem not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf
    {F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : F.obj (op T)) (t : T) :
    ¬ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc fun i => yoneda.map ((⊥ : (X i).Opens).ι) ≫ f i) := by
  intro hls
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (hls.imageSieve_mem s)
  obtain ⟨j, y, -⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq t
  obtain ⟨u, -⟩ := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  obtain ⟨i, x, -⟩ := CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.jointly_surjective'
    (Discrete.functor fun i => yoneda.obj ((⊥ : (X i).Opens) : Scheme.{u}))
    (op (𝒰.X j)) u
  exact (isEmpty_of_hom_bot (X := X i.as) x).elim y

/-- **The `⊥`-restricted atlas is NOT Zariski-locally surjective** — the instance-level
refutation, for an arbitrary chart family.

Given a test `T` with a point `t` and any section `s`, local surjectivity would make the image
sieve of `s` under `Sigma.desc` covering, hence would supply a Zariski cover of `T`; the cover
member through `t` is nonempty and carries a section of the coproduct presheaf lying in the
image, which `FunctorToTypes.jointly_surjective` resolves into a morphism to some
`(⊥ : (X i).Opens)` — making that member empty, contradicting the point it covers.

Note what does **not** enter: the class equation of the image sieve is discarded, so this is a
refutation of the *typing* at `⊥` and holds for any `f`.  No lane can escape it by changing
charts. -/
theorem not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : T) :
    ¬ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊥ : (X i).Opens)) :=
  not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf f T s t

/-! ## Discharging the refutation's own antecedents

The theorem above is an implication: it needs a test `T`, a section on it, and a point of `T`.
An implication whose antecedents nobody exhibits refutes nothing — it is consistent with there
being no such `T`.  This section exhibits them, so the `⊥` endpoint is dead outright and not
merely dead-if-something-exists. -/

/-- **`Spec k` carries a point.**  `k` is a field, hence nontrivial, hence its prime spectrum is
nonempty; the carrier of `Spec (.of k)` *is* that spectrum.

Stated because it is the antecedent the refutation needs and no other file in the seam
exhibits it. -/
theorem nonempty_specObj_of_field : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum k))

variable (C) in
/-- **A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf` over `Spec k`.**  A `Σ`-section at a test `T` is a pair: a
structure morphism `T ⟶ Spec k` and a degree-zero class on `Over.mk` of it.  Take the identity
morphism and the identity class — the trivial line bundle is always degree zero, so this needs
nothing about the curve.

The point of exhibiting it rather than quantifying over it: `pic0SigmaSheaf` could in principle
have been empty at every test, and then the refutation below would be about nothing. -/
def specSigmaSection : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
  ⟨𝟙 _, 1⟩

/-- **The `⊥` endpoint is dead, unconditionally** — the form the board should quote.

`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot` with all three of its antecedents discharged:
`Spec k` is the test, `specSigmaSection` the section, and `nonempty_specObj_of_field` the point.
Nothing is quantified but the chart family, and nothing about the curve, the divisor index or
`rep` enters at any step.

**What this settles and what it does not.**  Antecedent 1 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is
free at `⊥` with no hypothesis (`isChartUniv_bot`), so `⊥` was the one parameter value at which
the seam would have fired from nothing.  It cannot.  Combined with `isLocallySurjective_of_bot`
— inhabiting the binder at `⊥` would *give* unrestricted coverage — the endpoint is shut from
both directions.

It does **not** move the seam forward.  The pair (`huniv V`, coverage at `V`) has no measured
inhabitant at any `V`, and refuting two endpoints is not exhibiting an interior point. -/
theorem not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot' {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
    ¬ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊥ : (X i).Opens)) :=
  not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot f _ (specSigmaSection C)
    nonempty_specObj_of_field.some

/-! ## The consequence in the coordinates a coverage lane works in

Nobody proves the instance directly: a coverage lane proves `ChartsCoverLocally`
(`Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean`) and lets `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` convert.  So the
refutation is stated there too, otherwise a lane would have to notice the conversion itself. -/

/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` is false at `⊥`** — the refutation in the spelling a producer
actually attempts.

`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot'` composed with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Compare `not_coverageContainment_bot` (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`), which refutes
the `hcov` conjunct of the *coupled assembly* — a different and weaker statement, since it
leaves the instance binder untouched.  This one closes the binder. -/
theorem not_chartsCoverLocally_bot {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
    ¬ ChartsCoverLocally C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊥ : (X i).Opens)) := fun h =>
  not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot' f (isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc _ h)

/-- **`isLocallySurjective_of_bot` is VACUOUS, and this is the file's finding for that lane.**

`isLocallySurjective_of_bot` (`Pic0ChartVMonotone.lean`) proves that inhabiting the coverage
instance at `⊥` yields
unrestricted coverage, and reads that as "the `⊥` route is not cheap".  The reading is right;
the mechanism is stronger than advertised.  Its hypothesis is *exactly* the proposition refuted
above, so the theorem is true with an uninhabitable antecedent — it does not shut a cheap route,
there was never a route.

Recorded as a theorem rather than a remark because "this binder cannot be inhabited" and "this
binder is expensive to inhabit" price a lane's round very differently, and only the first is
true.  Nothing here criticises that file's proof, which is correct. -/
theorem false_of_isLocallySurjective_bot {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊥ : (X i).Opens))) :
    False :=
  not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot' f h

/-- **The control for the refutation: at `⊤` the restricted atlas INHERITS coverage.**

The converse of `isLocallySurjective_unrestricted` (`Pic0ChartVMonotone.lean`) at `V = ⊤`,
and the reason the refutation above is a fact about `⊥` rather than about the seam.  `⊤`'s
inclusion is an isomorphism, so `sigmaDesc_restrictChart_top` exhibits the `⊤`-restricted atlas as
an iso followed by the unrestricted one, and local surjectivity transfers by instance search.

**Read as the control it is.**  A `⊤` analogue of `not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot'`
would, through this, refute DAT-B coverage for every chart family — i.e. refute the project's own
target.  So the `⊥` endpoint is protected by something that *could* have come out differently, and
did not.  Note the iso is used here and nowhere in `Pic0ChartVMonotone.lean`, whose header records
that its own `⊤` results never need it; this is the statement that does. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_top {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc fun i => restrictChart (f i) (⊤ : (X i).Opens)) := by
  rw [sigmaDesc_restrictChart_top (C := C) f]
  infer_instance

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

The summary says B5/B6 are 'divRep/C9-gated' -- i.e. waiting on the divisor-representability chain. The true dependency runs the other way. Round 5 made everything ABOVE it unconditional (JacobianData.ofCharts), and the L9-L13 divisor-representability tail below it is nearly finished over a section variable. What is NOT merely unproved but arguably FALSE as currently phrased is B-6 itself:

 * divFamZar is by definition a quotient of LOCALLY CERTIFIED families (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224,:235);
 * the no-go (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31,:131) says it is BLIND to connected divisors meeting

 * so divFunctor C pi g is a PROPER SUBFUNCTOR of degree-g relative divisors, and the Abel map out
   of it cannot be Zariski-locally surjective onto Pic^0 -- the classes whose only witnesses are the
   invisible divisors are never hit.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS ROW: do not try to prove B-6 against divFunctor as it stands. First check which functor the surjectivity is stated against. Local surjectivity from a subfunctor that misses classes is FALSE, not hard, and no amount of work on the affine package or on U2 changes it. B-6 becomes provable only after the certificate route is widened -- repair R1 (twist by Aut(P^1), correct iff |P^1(k)| >= g+2) or R2 (generalise FinCoverData's piece type, field-uniform). That choice is the campaign's one live decision and it is recorded on AJCR.w4-rep.
